summary: Station A gripper fault coincides with bus over-power, sensor lag, and failed picks; simulated repair requires coordinated power, timing, and handoff changes.
limitations: Internal solenoid / hall-sensor / mechanical condition of Station A gripper is unknown from supplied simulation evidence.
Physical cause of Station A fault flag cannot be determined without physical inspection, which is outside simulator scope.
Long-term wear, wiring integrity, and real-machine safety are unknown.

fixes.title: Stagger arm surges and throttle belt
fixes.explanation: Interleaves arm surges to keep peak below 1.65 kW ceiling and throttles belt to reduce timing sensitivity; CHK-POWER-INTERLEAVE shows 1.554 kW with no trip.
fixes.tradeoff: Reduced throughput from 0.7 m/s throttling; alone does not resolve Station A fault or sensor lag assumption.

evaluation.note: This isolated change fails timing, station availability or the power envelope.

fixes.title: Hand off orders to Station B
fixes.explanation: Filters faulted Station A and routes all 8 orders to Station B; CHK-STATION-HANDOFF shows 8/8 routed.
fixes.tradeoff: Leaves power surge and timing mismatch unresolved, so simultaneous operation can still trip breaker or miss grasps.

evaluation.note: This isolated change fails timing, station availability or the power envelope.

fixes.title: Coordinate power, timing and handoff
fixes.explanation: Combines surge interleave, throttled belt-speed timing, Station B handoff, and telemetry filtering; repair twin packs 8/8 at 1.554 kW and challenger packs 8/8 despite telemetry errors. Isolated fixes can fail because power, lag, and fault interact.
fixes.tradeoff: Lower belt speed and reliance on Station B reduces redundancy and throughput.

evaluation.note: Passed the named judge and challenger scenarios on this snapshot.
